title: CoreHawk: My free Codex-developed game
author: JauntyMoon
selftext:
While I'm developing a game, mostly by hand, I started thikning about the PS3 game Warhawk and how much I miss playing it. I didn't want to spend time on a fully 3D version, so I built CoreHawk, which is a 2D, Warhawk-inspired game that takes place on a round 2D planet.

You can play single player with AI or play multiplayer. My wife and I like to play together on the same team in 40v40 deathmatches.

The server doesn't handle things like NAT traversal and I wouldn't reccoment exposing the srver to the internet, so LAN play is the best.

CoreHawk was built using Codex and GPT-6.1 Sol Medium.

My main approach was to give it a pretty detailed description of the game I wanted, then have it use imagegen to make a few mockups. I picked pieces I liked from each and iterated on them until I had something I liked.

Then I had it begin implementation (Godot + C#) using the mockup directly to pull sprites from. That made the sprites a bit messy, so we later did a clean up pass and I did some manual edits in Aseprite.

The agent struggled with good AI (which is still pretty bad) and efficient change tracking for sharing state across clients, so I had to do a lot of direction in both of those areas.

I spent 20 years as a professional software engineer in big tech, the last few heavily using LLMs for development. I was surprised that while the agents are great at building the game, they are really bad at making the game fun, even when copying existing ideas that have been used in many games.

I am enjoying the game producer and gameplay designer role.
